In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the higher-dimensional gluon operators have not been well studied and that their effects in the scattering processes considered are not yet well understood.
the dimension-six and dimension eight operators can be important for hadronic scattering at energies up to 10-20 TeV.
the dimension-eight operators are likely to be the dominant source of new physics in hadronic scattering at SSC energies, but that the dimension-six operators may be observable in certain cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dimension-six operators are already constrained to a few percent of their natural values by existing experimental data.

, while dimension-six operators can contribute at the percent level to partonic scattering processes at the SSC, dimension-eight operators are unlikely to have significant contributions to any process at the SSC.
the gluonic operators with dimensions six and eight can be used to probe physics at scales of order 10 ^{4} GeV and 10 ^{6} GeV, respectively, and that these scales may be accessible at the SSC.

dimension-eight gluon operators can be probed at the SSC in hadron-hadron and hadron-nucleus scattering at √s = 40 TeV.
